{{short description|Iraqi mathematician}}
'''Waleed Al-Salam''' (born 15 July 1926 in [[Baghdad]], [[British Mandate of Mesopotamia|Iraq]] – died 14 April 1996 in [[Edmonton, Canada]]) was a [[mathematician]] who introduced [[Al-Salam–Chihara polynomials]],  [[Al-Salam–Carlitz polynomials]], [[q-Konhauser polynomials]], and [[Al-Salam–Ismail polynomials]]. He was a [[Professor emeritus|Professor Emeritus]] at the [[University of Alberta]].

Born in Iraq, Baghdad, Al-Salam received his bachelor's degree in engineering physics (1950) and M.A. in mathematics (1951) from [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California Berkeley]]. He completed his education at [[Duke University|Duke]], receiving his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. for his dissertation on [[Bessel polynomials]] (1958).<ref>{{Cite journal|url = https://www.researchgate.net/publication/256736803|title = In Memoriam: Waleed Al-Salam|last = Chiahara|first = T.S.|date = November 1998|journal = Journal of Approximation Theory|doi = 10.1006/jath.1998.3301|access-date = 2016-01-29|doi-access = free}}</ref>
